title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Setting: E is an elliptic curve over a field k of characteristic not 2, with origin e. F_n = H^0(E, O(n·e)), and F_∞ = ∪ F_n = O(E − {e}) is the affine coordinate ring. The involution f ↦ f̌ is pullback by [−1], and F_n = F_n^+ ⊕ F_n^- is its eigenspace decomposition. J is the set (scheme) of non-zero 2-torsion points e_i. θ_ξ is the invariant derivation attached to ξ, a tangent vector at the origin (ξ ∈ t_E). On the previous page Grothendieck chose a 'Weierstrass function' ℘ ∈ F_2. The normalization is not the classical Laurent one. Instead the normalization is ℘'^2 = ℘^3 + a_1℘^2 + a_2℘ + a_3 with ℘' = θ_ξ℘, and ∏_{i∈J}(℘ − ℘(e_i)) = ℘^3 + a_1℘^2 + a_2℘ + a_3. In characteristic ≠ 3, the ℘ with a_1 = 0 form a complement W_E ≅ t_E^{⊗2} of F_1 = k·1 in F_2. The page opens by finishing the statement that the normalized Weierstrass elements correspond bijectively to elements of (t_E^{⊗2})^* (the choice of ℘ goes with the choice of ξ up to the weight-2 scaling). Corollary 3 states three things. (i) F_∞ ≅ k[P,P']/(P'^2 − (P^3 + a_1P^2 + a_2P + a_3)) via P ↦ ℘, P' ↦ ℘'. (ii) The involution corresponds to P' ↦ −P', P ↦ P. (iii) θ_ξ is induced by the derivation of k[P,P'] with θP = P' and θP' = ½(3P^2 + 2a_1P + a_2). This derivation kills the defining polynomial: θ(P'^2 − f(P)) = 2P'·½f'(P) − f'(P)P' = 0, so it preserves the ideal. The formula comes from differentiating ℘'^2 = f(℘) to get 2℘'θ(℘') = f'(℘)℘', then cancelling ℘' (legitimate since F_∞ is a domain). The concluding Remark says the explicit bases of F_n^± from (25') now allow the multiplication law and the derivation to be written out in terms of a_1, a_2, a_3. The next page goes the other way: given a_i with nonzero discriminant, Proj of the graded ring gives an elliptic curve, a double cover of P^1 branched at the roots of the cubic and at ∞. Overall purpose: an intrinsic, characteristic-free (char ≠ 2) Weierstrass normal form adapted to the 2-torsion and the tangent line. This prepares a description of the moduli stack of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2 as a quotient of the space of cubics y^2 = x^3 + a_1x^2 + a_2x + a_3 with Δ ≠ 0 by the affine group x ↦ u^2x + r, y ↦ u^3y.
errors: Formula (33) is written '℘' = ½(3℘^2 + 2a_1℘ + a_2)'. It should be θ_ξ(℘') = ℘'' = ½(3℘^2 + 2a_1℘ + a_2). This is a notational slip, since the left side as written is ℘' itself.
In (32) the second θ lacks the subscript ξ. On the next page the derivation is called Θ_δ, an inconsistent notation.
Minor point: the derivation does more than map the ideal into itself; it sends the generator to 0. This is correct but stronger than stated.

ideas.what: Coordinate ring of E minus origin as k[P,P']/(P'^2 − cubic), with the inverse map as P' ↦ −P'
ideas.modern_name: Weierstrass model / affine coordinate ring of an elliptic curve (y^2 = x^3 + a_2x^2 + a_4x + a_6 form)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weierstrass; standard, e.g. Tate, Deligne 'Courbes elliptiques: formulaire', Silverman

ideas.what: Invariant derivation on the Weierstrass ring: θx = y, θy = ½f'(x)
ideas.modern_name: Invariant vector field dual to the invariant differential dx/(2y) (or dx/y)

ideas.what: Normalizing ℘ intrinsically via 2-torsion and a tangent vector, with the a_i as symmetric functions of ℘(e_i)
ideas.modern_name: Weierstrass form adapted to 2-torsion / moduli via Legendre-type families in char ≠ 2
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur for moduli treatments

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, intrinsic but entirely standard rederivation of the Weierstrass coordinate ring and the invariant derivation. There is nothing beyond textbook material; its interest is only as a step in Grothendieck's own treatment of the moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'en corr. 1-1 avec les éléments de (t_E^{⊗2})^*' is correct.
In (32) the image shows Θ applied to P' with a corrected/overwritten letter; read it as θ_ξ P'.
In (33) the image reads ℘' on the left. This is mathematically ℘'' = θ_ξ(℘'), a slip in the original rather than a transcription error.

The crossed word above 'Remarque' is 'Exercice'. The transcription's duplicated phrase 'des bases explicites F_n^+ et F_n^- (25') des des [?] plus haut' should read: 'En termes des bases explicites des F_n^+ et F_n^- (25') données plus haut dans F_n = F_n^+ ⊕ F_n^-, on voit maintenant comment expliciter, en termes de a_1, a_2, a_3, la loi de multiplication, ainsi que [la dérivation]'.
In 'qui applique l'idéal', the first word is a crossed-out correction ('supplique'/'applique'); the reading 'applique' is right.
